newsitem.title: UK: IGC sees further rise in 1997-98 world wheat trade.
newsitem.headline: IGC sees further rise in 1997-98 world wheat trade.

text.p: The International Grains Council raised its estimate for 1997-98 world wheat trade to 95 million tonnes on Thursday from 94 million estimated last month, including an increase for Egypt which will make it the world's number one importer.
In its latest Grains Market Report, the IGC put 1996-97 trade at 93 million tonnes.
The IGC's higher forecast for Egyptian imports, up half a million tonnes to 7.0 million, means it will overtake Iran as the largest importer in 1997-98.
The IGC raised its estimate for Iran's imports to 5.0 million tonnes from the previous 4.5 million, but still leaving it under 1996-97's world-beating 6.7 million tonnes.

It also put half a million tonnes on Pakistan's imports, to 3.5 million tonnes, while China's imports were cut to 3.0 million tonnes from 4.0 million in the IGC's previous estimate. India's estimated imports were also cut, by 500,000 tonnes to 1.5 million.

There has been a shift in where the IGC expects the wheat to come from, with Australian exports cut by 1.5 million tonnes to 14 million and Argentine exports raised by 500,000 to nine million tonnes. But the biggest change is a 1.5 million tonne rise in the estimate for US exports to 29.0 million. --Christopher Lyddon, London newsroom +44 171 542 7928
